solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: What link attracts is a success (6)

blocks.note: a hyperlink on a web page is there to be pressed with the mouse
informal verb: a partnership or a show that takes off suddenly

annotation.surface: Someone praising a link, whether online or a person, for how it pulls people in.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half is a noun (the clicks a link gets), the second a verb (it clicks), so the same word serves two parts of speech.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: the mouse-presses a web link draws, and the informal verb for something suddenly working out.

entries.clue: Train station (5)

blocks.note: verb: to aim a gun at a target
noun: a person's rank or standing in society

annotation.surface: Two words that look like a railway phrase.
annotation.walkthrough: Read together the words are railway talk; apart, both are something else, a verb of aiming and a noun of rank.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: you level a weapon when you aim it, and your level is your standing in life.

entries.clue: Right person to join air force (9)

indicatorNotes.to join: CON is told to join the next piece, attaching itself in front

blocks.note: a Conservative, a person on the political right
a strain is a musical air

annotation.surface: A recruiter looking for the right candidate to join the air force.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Air force' reads as one service but splits: 'air' is a tune and 'force' is the definition. CON here is short for Conservative, the British right-wing party.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: compelling someone to act against their wishes.

entries.clue: When to rise up and change the world (6)

indicatorNotes.to rise up: in a down entry, rising means reading bottom to top, so AS becomes SA

annotation.surface: A revolutionary slogan about the moment to rise and remake the world.
annotation.walkthrough: The rallying cry hides the fact that 'the world' is not ours: a planet is a world, and a particular one is wanted.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: planets are often called worlds, and this is the ringed one.

entries.clue: Brief is useless for hearing in court (8)

indicatorNotes.for hearing: we want what is heard, not what is written

blocks.note: slang: it sucks = it is useless
CT is the abbreviation for court

annotation.surface: A barrister's brief dismissed as no good for a hearing in court.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brief' and 'hearing in court' pull toward law, but the brief is the adjective meaning short, and the hearing is the sound signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the adjective: expressed in few words.

entries.clue: What involves envy, idleness, as ultimately defined? (5,6,4)

annotation.definition: What involves envy, idleness, as ultimately defined?

indicatorNotes.involves: to involve is to entangle or roll up, so the letters that follow are mixed

annotation.surface: A catechism question: what list includes envy and sloth?
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and recipe: envy and idleness (sloth) really are on the list the answer names.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue asks which traditional list of vices includes envy and sloth.

entries.clue: Christmas trees, typically with presents one opens (8)

indicatorNotes.opens: I goes inside CONFERS, splitting it open

blocks.note: to confer is to present, as an honour

annotation.surface: Christmas trees with gifts beneath that someone is unwrapping.
annotation.walkthrough: The picture of opening presents is the misdirection: 'presents' is a verb, and 'opens' puts I into it.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by 'typically': Christmas trees are usually firs or spruces, cone-bearing evergreens.

entries.clue: Occupied home, but shed only every so often (2,3)

indicatorNotes.only every so often: take letters at regular intervals: the 2nd, 4th and 6th of BUTSHED

blocks.clueFragment: but shed only every so often

annotation.surface: A house that is lived in, while the garden shed barely gets used.
annotation.walkthrough: 'But' does double duty: in the surface it links, and its U is also the first of the letters taken.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as on the sign on a toilet door.

entries.clue: The people around one in revolution spot king being beheaded (9)

indicatorNotes.in revolution: revolving turns ZIT back to front
indicatorNotes.being beheaded: the king's name loses its first letter

annotation.surface: The mob at a revolution watching a king lose his head.
annotation.walkthrough: The French Revolution picture is apt, with a beheaded king and the citizens around him, but 'revolution' only turns a spot round.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the body of citizens of a state, taken together.

entries.clue: Tying in race, perhaps, in spite of landing second (4-6)

indicatorNotes.landing: S lands inside the race word, coming down in the middle of it

blocks.note: a race is one kind of event
even = in spite of, as in 'even so'

annotation.surface: A dead heat in a race, declared a tie though one horse seemed to land second.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'landing second' as finishing runner-up; it is S being landed. 'In spite of' for EVEN is loose but fair: 'even with the rain, we went'.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: when scores are tying, the sides are level, with nothing between them.

entries.clue: Capable of working on till (2,2)

blocks.note: fit for a task, or busy with it: what are you doing?

annotation.surface: Someone fit to keep serving at a shop till.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Till' looks like a cash register in the shop picture; here it is the preposition meaning until.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: equal to a job (and busy at it), and the preposition 'until', as in waiting up to midnight.

entries.clue: One used to press home satire, mostly (8)

indicatorNotes.mostly: all but the last letter of IRONY

annotation.surface: A satirist pressing home a point.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Press home' is an idiom for driving an argument through, but the definition stops at 'press' and 'home' starts the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the old stove-heated iron used to press clothes.

entries.clue: Peg delivers for those attending (6)

indicatorNotes.for those attending: those attending a talk are listeners, so we want the sound

blocks.note: to deliver someone is to set them loose

annotation.surface: A woman called Peg handing things out to the guests.
annotation.walkthrough: Peg looks like a name; it is the verb, as when a government pegs prices at a fixed level.
annotation.definitionFit: An economic sense: pegging prices or wages holds them fixed at their current level.

entries.clue: Fancy android eating sandwiches! (4)

indicatorNotes.sandwiches: the phrase holds the answer between other letters

blocks.note: the last two letters of android and the first two of eating

annotation.surface: A robot tucking into sandwiches, an absurd sight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches' looks like food for the android; it is the verb, meaning the words enclose the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the noun: a notion or whim that takes your fancy.

entries.clue: Utter depressed sound (9)

blocks.note: sound = all right, in good order

annotation.surface: Someone letting out a low, gloomy noise.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like a verb, to make a sound; it is the adjective meaning total.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the adjective meaning complete, as in utter nonsense.

entries.clue: Undo real reforms in economic area (8)

indicatorNotes.reforms: the letters are formed again in a new order

annotation.surface: A call to reverse genuine economic reforms.
annotation.walkthrough: Political reform is the picture, but 'reforms' just rebuilds the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal name for the eurozone, the group of countries sharing a single currency.

entries.clue: Trade union primarily helping work to calm down (7,2)

indicatorNotes.primarily: take the first letters of Trade and Union
indicatorNotes.work: the letters are worked into a new shape

annotation.surface: A union trying to help work cool down a dispute.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Work' reads as the noun, the job the union protects; here it is the command to rework TU plus HELPING.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: telling someone to relax and stop being so serious.

entries.clue: Outside of Hitchcock’s concern, maybe, director’s first cut (8)

indicatorNotes.cut: D, the first letter of director, is cut from Hitchcock's first name

blocks.note: a concern is a business, a company

annotation.surface: A film director's first cut judged outside Hitchcock's interests.
annotation.walkthrough: Hitchcock and 'director's first cut' make a film picture, but 'concern' is a company and the director only supplies D.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowed Italian phrase meaning in the open air, as with eating outside.

entries.clue: Had small snake under control? (8)

annotation.surface: Someone who kept a small pet snake in check.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Snake' is a verb, not the animal, and 'Had' is the slang sense of being tricked.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang sense: if you've been had, you've been cheated.

entries.clue: Provocative object briefly encapsulates unknown artist (4)

indicatorNotes.encapsulates: to encapsulate is to enclose as in a capsule, so the shortened goad wraps round the unknown

annotation.surface: A provocative piece of art that hides an unknown artist.
annotation.walkthrough: The goad is a spiked stick for driving cattle, hence a provocation.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Spanish painter of the Black Paintings.

entries.clue: Unconvincing copy (6)

blocks.note: adjective: weak, as an excuse can be
old office noun: a carbon copy on thin paper

annotation.surface: A reviewer's verdict on an unconvincing imitation.
annotation.walkthrough: The noun sense is old office jargon, from the thin paper such copies were typed on.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: a weak excuse, and a thin-paper duplicate of a document.

entries.clue: I do like a doctor who deals with stuff! (6)

blocks.note: one who does what others do, an imitator

annotation.surface: Someone who admires a doctor who gets things done.
annotation.walkthrough: Whimsically, someone who does like a doctor is a doctor's imitator. 'I do like' first reads as fondness; it means copying.
annotation.definitionFit: Stuff is an old word for woollen cloth, and this shopkeeper sells fabric.

entries.clue: Called for one to be put up in apartment perhaps (5)

indicatorNotes.to be put up: in a down entry, putting up reads EG bottom to top as GE
indicatorNotes.in: the reversed piece is lodged in the apartment, as a guest is put up in one

blocks.note: a pad is slang for a flat

annotation.surface: Someone summoned to put a guest up in their apartment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Called for' looks like one phrase, meaning summoned; the definition is just 'Called', and 'for one' gives EG.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: summoned over a loudspeaker or a pager.

entries.clue: Idle yet busy around university holiday period (8)

indicatorNotes.busy: the letters are all in motion
indicatorNotes.around: the rearranged letters go around U

annotation.surface: A student both idle and busy around the university holidays.
annotation.walkthrough: The contradiction of idle yet busy is the joke, and it fits the Christmas vacation.
annotation.definitionFit: An old word for the Christmas season, the midwinter holidays.

entries.clue: Dig instruction to strike in verse? The opposite! (5)

indicatorNotes.The opposite!: not DELE in V but V in DELE, the reverse of what 'in' says

blocks.note: dele is the proofreader's mark for 'delete'

annotation.surface: A poet told to go on strike, then told the reverse.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue first reads as DELE in V, then 'The opposite!' flips it so V goes in DELE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, literal (digging the ground) or figurative (digging into a subject).

entries.clue: A pair of blunders when one has to hide nothing is curious (4)

indicatorNotes.A pair of: a pair means two, so the blunder is written twice
indicatorNotes.has to hide nothing: the first blunder must conceal, so lose, its O, which is nothing

blocks.note: OG (own goal) with its O hidden
OG is an own goal, a football blunder

annotation.surface: Someone fascinated by a pair of mistakes where one conceals nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: An own goal (OG) is when a footballer scores against their own side. O stands for nothing, and 'one' says only the first OG loses it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: eagerly curious, all eyes and ears.

entries.clue: Knowing about feminist term good and well (10)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' as 'surrounding': the Knowing word wraps round the rest

blocks.note: a sly look is a knowing one

annotation.surface: Someone well versed in feminist jargon.
annotation.walkthrough: WIMMIN is a spelling some 1970s-80s feminists used to take 'men' out of women.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: things going well are going smoothly, like a swimmer through water.

entries.clue: Scholarly boss with ten certificates (8)

blocks.note: a boss is a raised stud, as on a shield
10 written as the letters I and O
U is a British film certificate (suitable for all), so two or more are Us

annotation.surface: A learned manager whose wall is covered in ten diplomas.
annotation.walkthrough: The boss is a raised stud, not a manager, and the certificates are British film ratings: U means suitable for all ages.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: given to study and learning.

entries.clue: You must keep getting gratuities endlessly for this reaction? (6)

indicatorNotes.must keep: YE holds the other piece inside
indicatorNotes.endlessly: TIPPED loses both its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A waiter overjoyed to keep on receiving tips.
annotation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark belongs to the answer: getting tip after tip is what makes you shout it.
annotation.definitionFit: The clue points at itself: the cry of delight you'd give on being tipped again and again.
